q: ____ is everything that is around us.
e: Environment is everything that is around us. Environment is the biological term this statement needs.

q: It can be living (____) or non-living (abiotic) things.
e: It can be living (biotic) or non-living (abiotic) things. Biotic factors are the living parts of the environment. Abiotic factors are the non-living parts of the environment.

q: It includes physical, chemical and other natural ____.
e: It includes physical, chemical and other natural forces. Physical, chemical, and other natural forces act on organisms all the time.

q: They constantly interact with it and ____ themselves to conditions in their environment.
e: They constantly interact with it and adapt themselves to conditions in their environment. Organisms adapt to the conditions around them or they fail to thrive. The environment is everything around an organism, biotic and abiotic.

q: Our environment has been classified into ____ major components.
e: Our environment has been classified into four major components. Four major environment components together are called the ecosphere.

q: These components together are known as the ____.
e: These components together are known as the Ecosphere. The ecosphere is hydrosphere, lithosphere, atmosphere, and biosphere together.

q: Hydrosphere includes all ____ bodies such as lakes, ponds, rivers, streams, oceans, etc.
e: Hydrosphere includes all water bodies such as lakes, ponds, rivers, streams, oceans, etc. Water is the essential solvent of cells and a raw material of photosynthesis. The hydrosphere is all water bodies: lakes, rivers, seas, and oceans.

q: Hydrosphere functions in a cyclic nature, which is termed as hydrological cycle or ____ cycle.
e: Hydrosphere functions in a cyclic nature, which is termed as hydrological cycle or water cycle. Water is the essential solvent of cells and a raw material of photosynthesis. The hydrosphere is all water bodies: lakes, rivers, seas, and oceans.

q: ____ means the mantle of rocks constituting the earth's crust.
e: Lithosphere means the mantle of rocks constituting the earth's crust. The lithosphere is the rock and soil crust of the earth. Rocks and soil belong to the lithosphere.

q: Lithosphere mainly contains soil, earth rocks, ____ etc.
e: Lithosphere mainly contains soil, earth rocks, mountain etc. The lithosphere is the rock and soil crust of the earth. Rocks and soil belong to the lithosphere.

q: Lithosphere is divided into ____ layers; crusts, mantle and core (outer and inner).
e: Lithosphere is divided into three layers; crusts, mantle and core (outer and inner). Dichotomous does not mean divided into three parts. The lithosphere is the rock and soil crust of the earth.

q: The cover of the air, that envelopes the earth is known as the ____.
e: The cover of the air, that envelopes the earth is known as the atmosphere. The atmosphere is the layer of gases around the earth.

q: Atmosphere is a thin layer which contains gases like oxygen, carbon dioxide, ____, etc., and which protects the solid earth and human beings from the harmful radiations of the sun.
e: Atmosphere is a thin layer which contains gases like oxygen, carbon dioxide, nitrogen, etc., and which protects the solid earth and human beings from the harmful radiations of the sun. Nitrogen is in amino acids and nucleic acids, but it is not in every biological molecule. Carbon dioxide is used in photosynthesis and produced by respiration and combustion.

q: There are ____ concentric layers within the atmosphere, which can be differentiated on the basis of temperature.
e: There are five concentric layers within the atmosphere, which can be differentiated on the basis of temperature. The atmosphere is the layer of gases around the earth.

q: These include the troposphere, the stratosphere, the mesosphere, the thermosphere and the ____.
e: These include the troposphere, the stratosphere, the mesosphere, the thermosphere and the exosphere. The exosphere is the outermost fringe of atmosphere, not the life layer.

q: Biosphere is otherwise known as the ____ layer, refers to all organisms on the earth's surface and their interaction with water and air.
e: Biosphere is otherwise known as the life layer, refers to all organisms on the earth's surface and their interaction with water and air. Biology is the science of life: plants, animals, and microorganisms. The biosphere is the global life layer where living things exist.

q: An ecosystem is functional units of a nature, where living organism interact among themselves and also with the surrounding ____ environment.
e: An ecosystem is functional units of a nature, where living organism interact among themselves and also with the surrounding physical environment. Biophysics uses physical laws; it is not the same as biochemistry. The environment is everything around an organism, biotic and abiotic.

q: The three major classes of ecosystems, referred to as '____', are terrestrial, freshwater, and marine ecosystems.
e: The three major classes of ecosystems, referred to as ' biomes ', are terrestrial, freshwater, and marine ecosystems. Dichotomous does not mean divided into three parts.

q: ____ are extremely dense ecosystems, which includes different types of plants and animals living in a very small area.
e: Rainforests are extremely dense ecosystems, which includes different types of plants and animals living in a very small area. Tropical rainforests hold huge biodiversity and recycle water and carbon quickly.

q: ____ is characterized by short growing seasons, cold temperatures, and poor soil.
e: Taiga is characterized by short growing seasons, cold temperatures, and poor soil. Taiga is the northern coniferous forest biome.

q: ____ usually have a moderately simple ecosystem, because of the very less living species found existing in these harsh conditions.
e: Tundra usually have a moderately simple ecosystem, because of the very less living species found existing in these harsh conditions. Tundra is a cold, treeless biome with a short growing season. An ecosystem is a community plus its physical environment, linked by energy and materials.

q: ____ include more animals living in the extremely hot temperature.
e: Deserts include more animals living in the extremely hot temperature. Deserts are biomes of very low rainfall and specialised xerophytes.

q: ____ supports more life as it is a mixed wetland and grassland ecosystem.
e: Savanna supports more life as it is a mixed wetland and grassland ecosystem. Savanna is tropical grassland with scattered trees and a wet-dry season. An ecosystem is a community plus its physical environment, linked by energy and materials.

q: Grasslands are areas where the vegetation are dominated by grasses and other ____ (non-woody) plants.
e: Grasslands are areas where the vegetation are dominated by grasses and other herbaceous (non-woody) plants. Herbaceous is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Grasslands occupy about ____% of the earth's surface.
e: Grasslands occupy about 24 % of the earth's surface. 24 is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Pond and ____ ecosystems are the two main freshwater ecosystems.
e: Pond and river ecosystems are the two main freshwater ecosystems. Dichotomous means divided into two parts, from Greek.

q: Freshwater ecosystems are actually the smallest of the three major classes of ecosystems which comprise ____% of the total of the Earth's surface.
e: Freshwater ecosystems are actually the smallest of the three major classes of ecosystems which comprise 1.8 % of the total of the Earth's surface. Dichotomous does not mean divided into three parts.

q: ____ water is salt water and fresh water mixed together.
e: Brackish water is salt water and fresh water mixed together. Brackish water is a mix of fresh and salt, as in many estuaries.

q: Ocean ecosystem is also known as the ____ ecosystems.
e: Ocean ecosystem is also known as the marine ecosystems. An ecosystem is a community plus its physical environment, linked by energy and materials.

q: ____ water ecosystem includes some tiny fish and coral living in shallow water close to the land.
e: Shallow water ecosystem includes some tiny fish and coral living in shallow water close to the land. An ecosystem is a community plus its physical environment, linked by energy and materials. Fish typically use gills; aquatic turtles more often use lungs and accessory surfaces.

q: Deep water ecosystem includes big and gigantic creatures, which live deep in the oceans and right at the ____ of the sea.
e: Deep water ecosystem includes big and gigantic creatures, which live deep in the oceans and right at the bottom of the sea. An ecosystem is a community plus its physical environment, linked by energy and materials.

q: ____ Ocean is the best example for the warm water ecosystem.
e: Pacific Ocean is the best example for the warm water ecosystem. An ecosystem is a community plus its physical environment, linked by energy and materials.

q: ____ are green plants which photosynthesise to produce food.
e: Producers are green plants which photosynthesise to produce food. Producers, mainly green plants, convert light to chemical energy.

q: ____ are animals that eat plants or other animals.
e: Consumers are animals that eat plants or other animals. Consumers get energy by eating other organisms.

q: The consumers that subsist on herbivores are ____ consumers while those that feed on primary consumers are secondary consumers and so on.
e: The consumers that subsist on herbivores are primary consumers while those that feed on primary consumers are secondary consumers and so on. Consumers get energy by eating other organisms.

q: ____ are organisms that break down dead material and help to recycle nutrients.
e: Decomposers are organisms that break down dead material and help to recycle nutrients. Decomposers such as bacteria and fungi break down dead material and recycle nutrients. An extra chromosome 21 produces Down's syndrome.

q: Decomposers are also termed as ____.
e: Decomposers are also termed as reducers. Decomposers such as bacteria and fungi break down dead material and recycle nutrients.

q: ____ factors are non-living physical or chemical factors.
e: Abiotic factors are non-living physical or chemical factors. Abiotic factors are the non-living parts of the environment.

q: Abiotic factors include climate, such as light intensity and duration, temperature and other weather conditions and water ____.
e: Abiotic factors include climate, such as light intensity and duration, temperature and other weather conditions and water availability. Abiotic factors are the non-living parts of the environment.

q: ____ factors are living organisms in the ecosystem.
e: Biotic factors are living organisms in the ecosystem. Biotic factors are the living parts of the environment. Biological molecules occur naturally inside living organisms, not in bare rock.

q: Biotic factors include availability of food and competition for food resources, predation, symbiosis, disease and presence of ____ insects.
e: Biotic factors include availability of food and competition for food resources, predation, symbiosis, disease and presence of pollinating insects. Predation is one biotic interaction that structures communities. Many insects breathe through a tracheal system, not lungs.

q: A ____ is the place where an organism lives.
e: A habitat is the place where an organism lives. Habitat is the biological term this statement needs.

q: All the organisms of a particular species found in an ecosystem at a certain time form the ____ of the species.
e: All the organisms of a particular species found in an ecosystem at a certain time form the population of the species. A population is all the individuals of one species in an area. An ecosystem is a community plus its physical environment, linked by energy and materials.

q: The populations of all species found in an ecosystem at a particular time form the ____.
e: The populations of all species found in an ecosystem at a particular time form the community. A community is all the populations living together in an area. An ecosystem is a community plus its physical environment, linked by energy and materials.

q: The simplest way of showing feeding relationships within an ecosystem is a ____ chain.
e: The simplest way of showing feeding relationships within an ecosystem is a food chain. Agriculture and husbandry both serve food production, but they are different practices. An ecosystem is a community plus its physical environment, linked by energy and materials.

q: In any food chain, the arrow (→) means '____'.
e: In any food chain, the arrow (→) means ' is eaten by '. A food chain is one linear feeding path from producer onward.

q: The direction of the arrows indicates the flow of ____ in the chain.
e: The direction of the arrows indicates the flow of energy in the chain. Living systems need a continual energy input to keep organised.

q: The different stages in a food chain are called ____ levels.
e: The different stages in a food chain are called trophic levels. Trophic levels are feeding steps in a food chain. A food chain is one linear feeding path from producer onward.

q: Another way of showing the feeding relationship with different food chains in an ecosystem is the food ____.
e: Another way of showing the feeding relationship with different food chains in an ecosystem is the food web. An ecosystem is a community plus its physical environment, linked by energy and materials.

q: ____ pyramids are diagrams that represent the relative amounts of organisms at each trophic level in a food chain.
e: Ecological pyramids are diagrams that represent the relative amounts of organisms at each trophic level in a food chain. A food chain is one linear feeding path from producer onward. Trophic levels are feeding steps in a food chain.

q: Pyramids of numbers represent the numbers of organisms in each trophic level in a food chain, irrespective of their ____.
e: Pyramids of numbers represent the numbers of organisms in each trophic level in a food chain, irrespective of their mass. A food chain is one linear feeding path from producer onward. Trophic levels are feeding steps in a food chain.

q: Pyramids of biomass show the total mass of the organisms in each trophic level, irrespective of their ____.
e: Pyramids of biomass show the total mass of the organisms in each trophic level, irrespective of their numbers. Trophic levels are feeding steps in a food chain.

q: The total biomass ____ at each trophic level.
e: The total biomass decreases at each trophic level. Trophic levels are feeding steps in a food chain.

q: Photosynthesis 'fixes' sunlight energy into ____ energy such as glucose and starch.
e: Photosynthesis 'fixes' sunlight energy into chemical energy such as glucose and starch. Biochemistry looks at chemical substances and chemical processes in cells. Photosynthesis builds glucose and oxygen from carbon dioxide and water using chlorophyll and light.

q: ____ releases energy from organic compounds such as glucose.
e: Respiration releases energy from organic compounds such as glucose. Respiration releases energy from food; do not mix it up with just breathing. Glucose is the hexose sugar made in photosynthesis and burned in respiration.

q: Almost all other biological processes use the energy released in ____.
e: Almost all other biological processes use the energy released in respiration. Respiration releases energy from food; do not mix it up with just breathing.

q: If the energy released in respiration is used to produce new cells, then the energy remains '____' in molecules in that organism.
e: If the energy released in respiration is used to produce new cells, then the energy remains ' fixed ' in molecules in that organism. Respiration releases energy from food; do not mix it up with just breathing.

q: If the energy released in respiration is used for other processes then it will, eventually escape as ____ from the organism.
e: If the energy released in respiration is used for other processes then it will, eventually escape as heat from the organism. Respiration releases energy from food; do not mix it up with just breathing.

q: Energy is therefore ____ from food chains and webs at each trophic level.
e: Energy is therefore lost from food chains and webs at each trophic level. Food chains show how chemical energy flows from producers to consumers. Trophic levels are feeding steps in a food chain.

q: Only about ____% of the energy entering a trophic level is passed on to the next trophic level.
e: Only about 10 % of the energy entering a trophic level is passed on to the next trophic level. Trophic levels are feeding steps in a food chain.

q: This is why food chains may not have more than ____ trophic levels.
e: This is why food chains may not have more than five trophic levels. Trophic levels are feeding steps in a food chain.

q: ____ is the effect of undesirable changes in our surroundings that have harmful effects on plants, animals and human beings.
e: Pollution is the effect of undesirable changes in our surroundings that have harmful effects on plants, animals and human beings. Pollution is harmful extra material or energy put into the environment.

q: A substance which causes pollution is called a ____.
e: A substance which causes pollution is called a pollutant. A pollutant is a substance that harms air, water, soil, or living things. Pollution is harmful extra material or energy put into the environment.

q: Pollutants damage the quality of air, water, and ____.
e: Pollutants damage the quality of air, water, and land. Land is the biological term this statement needs.

q: The ____ major types of pollution are: Air Pollution, water pollution, land pollution, light pollution, noise pollution, Thermal pollution and radioactive pollution.
e: The seven major types of pollution are: Air Pollution, water pollution, land pollution, light pollution, noise pollution, Thermal pollution and radioactive pollution. Older schemes listed seven ranks; adding domain makes eight. Pollution is harmful extra material or energy put into the environment.

q: ____ pollution is the release of harmful contaminants into the atmosphere.
e: Air pollution is the release of harmful contaminants into the atmosphere. Air of the atmosphere supplies oxygen and carbon dioxide for life. The atmosphere is the layer of gases around the earth.

q: This contamination can be caused by industries, car exhaust, dust, volcanoes and ____.
e: This contamination can be caused by industries, car exhaust, dust, volcanoes and wildfires. Wildfires is the biological term this statement needs.

q: ____ pollution is the contamination of water bodies usually caused due to human activities.
e: Water pollution is the contamination of water bodies usually caused due to human activities. Water is the essential solvent of cells and a raw material of photosynthesis. Lakes, ponds, rivers, streams, and oceans are water bodies of the hydrosphere.

q: Water pollution causes disease such as dysentery, typhoid, jaundice and ____, etc.
e: Water pollution causes disease such as dysentery, typhoid, jaundice and fever, etc. Pollution is harmful extra material or energy put into the environment.

q: ____ pollution is the degradation of land due to the presence of chemicals or other man-made substances in the soil.
e: Land pollution is the degradation of land due to the presence of chemicals or other man-made substances in the soil. Pollution is harmful extra material or energy put into the environment.

q: Land pollution causes soil erosion progress, shift of animals' habitats and adverse affects on the health of animals and ____.
e: Land pollution causes soil erosion progress, shift of animals' habitats and adverse affects on the health of animals and humans. Pollution is harmful extra material or energy put into the environment. Medicine and veterinary science restore and maintain health.

q: ____ pollution is the continuous noise in the surrounding that disrupts the natural balance.
e: Noise pollution is the continuous noise in the surrounding that disrupts the natural balance. Continuous culture keeps adding nutrients and taking product for a long run. Pollution is harmful extra material or energy put into the environment.

q: Noise pollution causes high blood pressure, heart disease, sleep disturbances, and ____.
e: Noise pollution causes high blood pressure, heart disease, sleep disturbances, and stress. Pollution is harmful extra material or energy put into the environment.

q: ____ pollution is the increase of temperature caused by human activities.
e: Thermal pollution is the increase of temperature caused by human activities. Pollution is harmful extra material or energy put into the environment.

q: A common cause of thermal pollution is the use of water as a ____ by power plants and industrial manufacturers.
e: A common cause of thermal pollution is the use of water as a coolant by power plants and industrial manufacturers. Pollution is harmful extra material or energy put into the environment.

q: ____ pollution is the presence of anthropogenic and artificial light in the night environment.
e: Light pollution is the presence of anthropogenic and artificial light in the night environment. Light supplies the energy that chlorophyll captures for photosynthesis. The environment is everything around an organism, biotic and abiotic.

q: ____ pollution is the emission of high energy particles or radioactive substance into air, water or land due to human activities in the form of radioactive waste.
e: Radioactive pollution is the emission of high energy particles or radioactive substance into air, water or land due to human activities in the form of radioactive waste. Pollution is harmful extra material or energy put into the environment.

q: Radioactive pollution carries serious health risks such as ____ or death.
e: Radioactive pollution carries serious health risks such as cancer or death. Cancer is uncontrolled cell division after control checkpoints fail. Pollution is harmful extra material or energy put into the environment.

q: A ____ cycle is a repeated pathway of a particular nutrient or element from the physical environment to living organisms and back to the environment.
e: A nutrient cycle is a repeated pathway of a particular nutrient or element from the physical environment to living organisms and back to the environment. Biological molecules occur naturally inside living organisms, not in bare rock. The environment is everything around an organism, biotic and abiotic.

q: The six main nutrient cycles of an ecosystem are carbon cycle, hydrogen cycle, oxygen cycle, ____ cycle, phosphorous cycle and sulphur cycle.
e: The six main nutrient cycles of an ecosystem are carbon cycle, hydrogen cycle, oxygen cycle, nitrogen cycle, phosphorous cycle and sulphur cycle. Nitrogen is in amino acids and nucleic acids, but it is not in every biological molecule. The nitrogen cycle depends on fixing, nitrifying, and denitrifying microbes.

q: The ____ cycle is the biogeochemical cycle whereby nitrogen is converted into various chemical forms as it circulates among atmosphere, terrestrial, and marine ecosystems.
e: The nitrogen cycle is the biogeochemical cycle whereby nitrogen is converted into various chemical forms as it circulates among atmosphere, terrestrial, and marine ecosystems. Nitrogen is in amino acids and nucleic acids, but it is not in every biological molecule. The nitrogen cycle depends on fixing, nitrifying, and denitrifying microbes.

q: Nitrogen gas constitutes ____% of the atmosphere.
e: Nitrogen gas constitutes 78 % of the atmosphere. The atmosphere is the layer of gases around the earth. Nitrogen is in amino acids and nucleic acids, but it is not in every biological molecule.

q: The $N_2$ gas is ____ and unable to used by plants and animals.
e: The N2 gas is inert and unable to used by plants and animals. Inert is the biological term this statement needs.

q: ____ bacteria can convert this nitrogen gas into compounds that can be assimilated by plants and animals.
e: Chemoautotrophic bacteria can convert this nitrogen gas into compounds that can be assimilated by plants and animals. Nitrogen is in amino acids and nucleic acids, but it is not in every biological molecule.

q: Nitrogen cycle consists of four main steps: Nitrogen fixation, ____, nitrification, and denitrification.
e: Nitrogen cycle consists of four main steps: Nitrogen fixation, ammonification, nitrification, and denitrification. Ammonification is microbes releasing ammonia from dead organic nitrogen. The nitrogen cycle depends on fixing, nitrifying, and denitrifying microbes.

q: The first stage of the nitrogen cycle is the conversion of inert nitrogen gas ($N_2$) into ____ ($NH_3$).
e: The first stage of the nitrogen cycle is the conversion of inert nitrogen gas (N2) into ammonia (NH3). The nitrogen cycle depends on fixing, nitrifying, and denitrifying microbes. The nitrogen cycle moves nitrogen between air, soil, microbes, and living tissue.

q: This reaction is catalysed by the enzyme ____, which is produced by nitrogen-fixing bacteria in the soil.
e: This reaction is catalysed by the enzyme nitrogenase, which is produced by nitrogen-fixing bacteria in the soil. Nitrogenase is the enzyme that fixes nitrogen gas into a usable form. Nitrogen is in amino acids and nucleic acids, but it is not in every biological molecule.

q: ____ is found living freely in the soil, while Rhizobium forms a mutualistic association with the roots of legumes.
e: Azotobacter is found living freely in the soil, while Rhizobium forms a mutualistic association with the roots of legumes. Azotobacter is a free-living nitrogen-fixing bacterium. Legumes host nitrogen-fixing Rhizobium in root nodules.

q: Rhizobium forms nodules within the plant roots and supplies ammonia to the plant in exchange for ____.
e: Rhizobium forms nodules within the plant roots and supplies ammonia to the plant in exchange for carbohydrates. Carbohydrates are sugars and polymers of sugars used for energy and structure. Roots may use air spaces or aerenchyma when soil oxygen is low.

q: Ammonia ($NH_3$) becomes ____ ($NH_4^+$) when mixed with water, and this can be used by plants.
e: Ammonia (NH3) becomes ammonium (NH4^+) when mixed with water, and this can be used by plants. Ammonium is a form of nitrogen plants can take up after ammonification or fixation.

q: Ammonia can also be produced from organic sources of nitrogen when broken down by ____.
e: Ammonia can also be produced from organic sources of nitrogen when broken down by decomposers. Decomposers such as bacteria and fungi break down dead material and recycle nutrients. Nitrogen is in amino acids and nucleic acids, but it is not in every biological molecule.

q: As a plant or animal decays, ____ will decompose organic materials to produce ammonia (and ammonium ions).
e: As a plant or animal decays, saprotrophs will decompose organic materials to produce ammonia (and ammonium ions). Saprotrophs digest dead organic matter outside their cells, then absorb it. Ammonium is a form of nitrogen plants can take up after ammonification or fixation.

q: This process is known as ____ and releases ammonium ions into the soil which can be absorbed by plants.
e: This process is known as ammonification and releases ammonium ions into the soil which can be absorbed by plants. Ammonification is microbes releasing ammonia from dead organic nitrogen. Ammonium is a form of nitrogen plants can take up after ammonification or fixation.

q: Nitrification is the conversion of ammonium ions into ____ ($NO_2^-$) and nitrates ($NO_3^-$) by nitrifying bacteria in the soil.
e: Nitrification is the conversion of ammonium ions into nitrites (NO2^-) and nitrates (NO3^-) by nitrifying bacteria in the soil. Nitrites are the middle step as ammonia is oxidised toward nitrate. Ammonium is a form of nitrogen plants can take up after ammonification or fixation.

q: ____ converts ammonium ions into nitrites, while Nitrobacter can convert the nitrites into nitrates.
e: Nitrosomonas converts ammonium ions into nitrites, while Nitrobacter can convert the nitrites into nitrates. Nitrosomonas oxidises ammonia to nitrite in nitrification. Nitrites are the middle step as ammonia is oxidised toward nitrate.

q: Nitrification reactions require ____ and hence soil must be well aerated to ensure a rich supply of nitrites and nitrates.
e: Nitrification reactions require oxygen and hence soil must be well aerated to ensure a rich supply of nitrites and nitrates. Oxygen is released by photosynthesis and used as the final electron acceptor in aerobic respiration. Nitrites are the middle step as ammonia is oxidised toward nitrate.

q: Denitrification is a chemical reduction process that converts nitrates ($NO_3^-$) into ____ gas ($N_2$).
e: Denitrification is a chemical reduction process that converts nitrates (NO3^-) into nitrogen gas (N2). Nitrogen is in amino acids and nucleic acids, but it is not in every biological molecule. Chromosome number is reduced in meiosis I, not in mitosis.

q: Denitrification is carried out by denitrifying bacteria (e.g. Pseudomonas denitrificans) in the absence of ____.
e: Denitrification is carried out by denitrifying bacteria (e.g. Pseudomonas denitrificans) in the absence of oxygen. Oxygen is released by photosynthesis and used as the final electron acceptor in aerobic respiration.

q: ____ is an important element for all living organisms.
e: Phosphorus is an important element for all living organisms. Biological molecules occur naturally inside living organisms, not in bare rock.

q: Phosphorus is a component of biological molecules such as RNA, DNA, phospholipids, and adenosine triphosphate (____).
e: Phosphorus is a component of biological molecules such as RNA, DNA, phospholipids, and adenosine triphosphate (ATP). ATP is the cell's immediate energy currency. DNA carries the genetic code in a double helix of nucleotides.

q: Phosphorus cycle is a very ____ process.
e: Phosphorus cycle is a very slow process. Slow is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Phosphorus is found in ____.
e: Phosphorus is found in rocks. Rocks and soil belong to the lithosphere.

q: Phosphorus comes out from the rocks by ____.
e: Phosphorus comes out from the rocks by weathering. Weathering of rock releases mineral nutrients into soil. Rocks and soil belong to the lithosphere.

q: Rain and other sources of erosion result in phosphorus being washed into the ____.
e: Rain and other sources of erosion result in phosphorus being washed into the soil. Soil is the biological term this statement needs.

q: In the soil, plants, fungi, and ____ are able to absorb phosphorus and grow.
e: In the soil, plants, fungi, and microorganisms are able to absorb phosphorus and grow. Microorganisms are microscopic living things such as bacteria, protozoa, and many fungi.

q: When the plants and animals die, they are decomposed by ____.
e: When the plants and animals die, they are decomposed by microorganisms. Microorganisms are microscopic living things such as bacteria, protozoa, and many fungi.

q: ____ is an essential component of living organisms.
e: Sulphur is an essential component of living organisms. Biological molecules occur naturally inside living organisms, not in bare rock.

q: Sulphur is a constituent part of many proteins and enzyme ____.
e: Sulphur is a constituent part of many proteins and enzyme cofactors. Proteins are polymers of amino acids with many structural and catalytic jobs. Enzymes are biological catalysts that speed reactions without being used up.

q: Sulphur in the air and soil may be oxidised to form ____ ($SO_4^{2-}$).
e: Sulphur in the air and soil may be oxidised to form sulphates (SO4^2-). Sulphates is the biological term this statement needs.

q: ____ are reduced by plants and bacteria.
e: Sulphates are reduced by plants and bacteria. Sulphates is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Hence, sulphur becomes incorporated into ____ molecules.
e: Hence, sulphur becomes incorporated into organic molecules. Organic biological molecules all contain carbon.

q: Sulphur within the soil can also be mineralised into inorganic forms and incorporated with ____ (e.g. iron sulphide).
e: Sulphur within the soil can also be mineralised into inorganic forms and incorporated with metals (e.g. Iron sulphide). Inorganic substances may lack carbon chains; they are not the carbon-based macromolecules of cells.

q: When fossil fuels are burnt, sulphur is released as sulphur ____ ($SO_2$).
e: When fossil fuels are burnt, sulphur is released as sulphur dioxide (SO2). Dioxide is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Sulphur dioxide is one of the main components of ____ rain.
e: Sulphur dioxide is one of the main components of acid rain. Acid is the biological term this statement needs.

q: A ____ is any substance that is taken into the body that alters or influences chemical reactions in the body.
e: A drug is any substance that is taken into the body that alters or influences chemical reactions in the body. Drug is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Drugs are very useful and helpful to a sick person if prescribed by a ____.
e: Drugs are very useful and helpful to a sick person if prescribed by a doctor. Doctor is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Penicillin, for example, is an ____ and cure bacterial infections such as pneumonia, gonorrhoea, syphillis etc.
e: Penicillin, for example, is an antibiotic and cure bacterial infections such as pneumonia, gonorrhoea, syphillis etc. Antibiotics kill or stop bacteria; they do not work on viruses. Penicillin is an antibiotic originally from a fungus.

q: ____ is a sedative drug used as a painkiller.
e: Aspirin is a sedative drug used as a painkiller. Aspirin is a painkiller used as a medicine, an applied-biology product.

q: Aspirin numbs the part of the brain sensitive to pain such as headaches and ____.
e: Aspirin numbs the part of the brain sensitive to pain such as headaches and toothaches. Aspirin is a painkiller used as a medicine, an applied-biology product.

q: Drug abuse or substance abuse refers to the use of certain chemicals for the purpose of creating pleasurable effects on the ____.
e: Drug abuse or substance abuse refers to the use of certain chemicals for the purpose of creating pleasurable effects on the brain. Brain is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Drug abuse is the use of illegal drugs or the use of prescription or nonprescription drugs for purposes other than those for which they are meant to be used, or in large ____.
e: Drug abuse is the use of illegal drugs or the use of prescription or nonprescription drugs for purposes other than those for which they are meant to be used, or in large amounts. Amounts is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Drug abuse may lead to social, physical, emotional, and ____-related problems.
e: Drug abuse may lead to social, physical, emotional, and job -related problems. Job is the biological term this statement needs.

q: An example of a narcotic drug is ____ to which people can become seriously addicted.
e: An example of a narcotic drug is heroin to which people can become seriously addicted. Heroin is a narcotic drug with strong withdrawal effects; it is not a biology tool.

q: Heroin is a strong sedative so that if it is abruptly withdrawn, the addicts would experience unpleasant ____ symptoms such as insomnia, muscle cramps, sweating, headaches, diarrhoea, vomiting and nausea.
e: Heroin is a strong sedative so that if it is abruptly withdrawn, the addicts would experience unpleasant withdrawal symptoms such as insomnia, muscle cramps, sweating, headaches, diarrhoea, vomiting and nausea. Heroin is a narcotic drug with strong withdrawal effects; it is not a biology tool.

q: An overdose of heroin causes ____ or death.
e: An overdose of heroin causes coma or death. Heroin is a narcotic drug with strong withdrawal effects; it is not a biology tool.

q: Many addicts turn to ____ because they need money to supply themselves with the regular doses.
e: Many addicts turn to crime because they need money to supply themselves with the regular doses. Crime is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Drug addiction may also lead to the spreading of ____ (Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome).
e: Drug addiction may also lead to the spreading of AIDS (Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome). AIDS is caused by HIV, a virus, so antibiotics are not the cure.

q: This is possible if other drug addicts share the ____ of an infected person.
e: This is possible if other drug addicts share the needle of an infected person. Needle is the biological term this statement needs.

q: People can easily become addicted to drinking ____ just as they do to drug taking.
e: People can easily become addicted to drinking alcohol just as they do to drug taking. Alcohol is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Excessive consumption of alcohol leads to physical, psychological and social ____.
e: Excessive consumption of alcohol leads to physical, psychological and social disabilities. Disabilities is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Alcohol affects the nervous system, reducing self-control and ____ time to a stimulus.
e: Alcohol affects the nervous system, reducing self-control and reaction time to a stimulus. Reaction is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Drinking large quantities of alcohol over a number of years can have serious effects on ____.
e: Drinking large quantities of alcohol over a number of years can have serious effects on health. Medicine and veterinary science restore and maintain health.

q: Excessive alcohol consumption can lead to stomach ulcers, heart disease and ____ damage.
e: Excessive alcohol consumption can lead to stomach ulcers, heart disease and brain damage. Brain is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Socially, heavy drinking may lead to family disruption and traffic and other ____.
e: Socially, heavy drinking may lead to family disruption and traffic and other accidents. Accidents is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Tobacco smoke contains a mixture of harmful chemical substances such as nicotine, tar, carbon monoxide and smoke ____.
e: Tobacco smoke contains a mixture of harmful chemical substances such as nicotine, tar, carbon monoxide and smoke particles. Particles is the biological term this statement needs.

q: When inhaled some of these chemical substances either are deposited in lungs or enter the blood ____.
e: When inhaled some of these chemical substances either are deposited in lungs or enter the blood stream. Lungs are the main terrestrial organs of gas exchange.

q: Consequently, smoking will lead to the development of chronic bronchitis, emphysema and lung ____.
e: Consequently, smoking will lead to the development of chronic bronchitis, emphysema and lung cancer. Cancer is uncontrolled cell division after control checkpoints fail.

q: Smoking also increases the risk of ____ disease.
e: Smoking also increases the risk of heart disease. Heart is the biological term this statement needs.

q: If a pregnant women smokes, the chemical substances in the tobacco may interfere with the baby's development in the ____.
e: If a pregnant women smokes, the chemical substances in the tobacco may interfere with the baby's development in the womb. Womb is the biological term this statement needs.

q: As a result of maternal smoking, the baby may be born ____ or even born dead.
e: As a result of maternal smoking, the baby may be born underweight or even born dead. Underweight is the biological term this statement needs.
